entry.name: Force-Vision (Li et al., ICLR 2024)
entry.title: Learning to Jointly Understand Visual and Tactile Signals
entry.summary: A person wearing a knitted full-hand pressure glove (16x16 readouts over palm and fingers, calibrated to newtons with a UR5e) squeezes, holds and presses 89 articulated tools (scissors, sprayers, staplers, clips) while a webcam records the hand-object scene; 150,000 frames of paired force maps and RGB, plus a canonical photo of each object.
entry.hand: knitted pressure glove built after Sundaram et al. 2019 (STAG method), one hand

sensor.note: 16x16 grid of pressure readouts per frame, stored as a 2D heatmap; calibrated to force with a UR5e arm.

scale.text: 150,000 frames, 89 object instances in 4+ categories, manipulations squeeze, hold and press; train 123,561 frames (81 objects), test 21,000 frames

entry.access: The project site's 'Download Data' links a Google Drive file (d256.zip) whose page opens without sign-in; size not shown, files not opened (checked 2026-11-24).
caveats: The introduction says 2,000,000 paired frames; the dataset section says 150,000 frames (123,561 train, 21,000 test). The smaller figure is used here.
Glove maker, sampling rate and number of wearers are not stated; the glove follows the knitted design of Sundaram et al. 2019 but with a 16x16 readout grid.
No hand pose is recorded; the second modality is a single webcam video plus a static photo of each object.
unconfirmed: taxels_per_hand 256 is the 16x16 readout grid stated in the paper; the physical sensor count of the glove is not given.
principle piezoresistive is assumed from the cited knitted-glove design (Sundaram et al. 2019), which uses a piezoresistive film; the paper only says 'embroidery-based'.
tasks 3 counts the manipulation types named in the latent-space figure (squeeze, hold, press).
Whether d256.zip holds the full 150,000-frame release was not checked; files not opened.
